edges.effect_quant: A 2019 systematic review found iron deficiency rose from 12.9% pre-RYGB to 24.5% post-RYGB, while a large 10-year cohort found iron deficiency in 51.3% of patients after surgery.
edges.mechanism: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass reduces gastric acidity and bypasses the duodenum and proximal jejunum, where iron absorption is normally concentrated. Reduced intake of iron-rich foods and poor tolerance of oral iron after surgery can compound the malabsorptive effect over time.
edges.summary: Iron deficiency is one of the most reproducible long-term complications of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Systematic review, large retrospective cohort data, and longitudinal micronutrient follow-up all show that iron depletion becomes more common as follow-up lengthens, especially in women and in those with inadequate supplementation.
edges.caveats: Absolute incidence depends on baseline iron status, sex, menstrual blood loss, supplementation protocol, and laboratory definitions. This edge is strongest for Roux-en-Y gastric bypass specifically and should not be generalized to sleeve gastrectomy without qualification.
